'''Sunday''' is a feastday and festival at midsummer, and is celebrated in many parts of the world. This is the summer solstice, the longest day of the year.

Sunday falls within the month of [[Amadaine]], although it is a separate day not part of the month.<ref>''[[The World of Robert Jordan's The Wheel of Time]]'', chapter 31: Sunday "comes annually in Amadaine, but is not a day of that month."</ref>

== Observance in the Two Rivers ==
In the [[Two Rivers]], Sunday is a day of feasting, dancing and wearing your best clothes. Rand recalls [[Whatley Eldin]] painting his wagon in bright colors and intricate scrollwork in preparation for Sunday. Young men compete in competitions of speed, strength and skill on Sunday, including archery and quarterstaff.

If a woman is interested in a man and wants him to know it, she might put flowers in his hair at Sunday, or she makes a point of asking him and no once else to dance.<ref>{{4|6}}, Egwene to Elayne: "In the Two Rivers ... if a woman wants a man to know she is interested in him, she puts flowers in his hair at Bel Time or Sunday. Or she might embroider a feastday shirt for him any time. Or make a point of asking him to dance and no one else."</ref>

== Trivia ==
* When Perrin and [[Egwene al'Vere|Egwene]] are traveling alone and hiding from Whitecloaks, Egwene asks Perrin if he'll dance with her on Sunday if they're home by then, and he says he will.<ref>{{1|34}}</ref>
* Every year on Sunday, Rand would put flowers on [[Kari al'Thor|his mother]]'s grave.<ref>{{1|1}}: "She had been an outlander, and Rand remembered little of her aside from a smiling face, though he did put flowers on her grave every year, at Bel Tine, in the spring, and at Sunday, in the summer."</ref>
